sections.html:
On Colorado's Western Slope, Delta County was split off from Gunnison County on February 11, 1883. The city of Delta is both seat and biggest town, and owners tend to place their homes in Orchard City, Cedaredge, Hotchkiss or Paonia. The 2020 count was 31,196 people and the July 2025 estimate is 32,178.

Owners live in 77.9% of homes here, and the median value of those homes is $343,200, a countywide midpoint. A small house in Delta and an orchard property near Paonia will land far from it, and your tax bill follows your own property's assessed value. A house in the city, a farm lot near Hotchkiss and a place in Cedaredge can also sit in different tax areas with different mill levies, so the address matters more than the county name.

sections.h2: How Delta County calculates the bill
sections.html:
Delta County takes actual value, multiplies by an assessment rate, and then applies each taxing authority's mill levy for the tax area your property is in. In order:

  1. Use on January 1 decides how the Assessor classifies the property.
  2. Houses are valued from comparable sales alone, and the 2025 and 2026 tax years use sales from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024.
  3. Since 2025 houses carry two assessment rates, with schools on one and other local governments on the other. The county's own 2025 illustration shows 6.25 percent and 7.05 percent respectively.
  4. Every taxing authority sets its mill levy by dividing the revenue it needs by the assessed value within its boundary.

The money stays local and none of it pays for state services. Levies differ between tax areas, so your own bill is the only reliable number.

Bills cover the prior year. Choose a single April 30 payment or two halves.

EventDate
Notice of Valuation, real propertyBy May 1
Protest of real property valueBy June 8
First half or full payment optionLast day of February, or April 30 in full
Second halfJune 15
Appeal to County Board of EqualizationBy July 15
Board hearings finishAugust 5
Further appealWithin 30 days of the decision

Real property is revalued in odd-numbered years. Taxes of $25 or less must be paid in full by April 30.

Contact the Assessor any time from January 1 to June 8, whether by phone, in person or in the mail. Going in person works best, and the county urges owners to appeal early.

  • Gather evidence from the Assessor's sales books and neighborhood sales lists.
  • Explain why the number is wrong and name the value you think is right.
  • The Assessor answers by the last working day of June and may visit the property to verify size and finish.
  • Still disagree? The County Board of Equalization takes appeals through July 15. Its members are the county commissioners, and you hear back within five working days.

Earlier tax years are off the table in this process, and the Assessor can't weigh sales after June 30, 2024. Phone the Assessor to confirm dates before filing.

Value is the Assessor's job and billing is the Treasurer's. The Assessor works from 375 W. 6th St., Delta (970-874-2120) on weekdays, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., though hours are shorter during the protest season of May 1 through June 8.

The Treasurer is at 501 Palmer Street, Suite 202, Delta (970-874-2135), with a lunch break between 1 p.m. and 2 p.m. Payments are taken there, at the County Annex at 196 W. Hotchkiss Avenue in Hotchkiss, through the mail to PO Box 580, Grand Junction, or online with GovPros. A mailed payment is proven only by a USPS postmark.

Deeds go to the Clerk and Recorder, 501 Palmer Street, Suite 211, 970-874-2150. Recording is $43 per document.

Late tax collects one percent interest every month, and a partial month counts as a whole one (C.R.S. 39-10-104.5). The clock starts March 1 for a missed first half, June 16 for a missed second half and May 1 for a missed full payment.

There is a grace period on the first half. Pay within 30 days of the statement being mailed and no delinquent interest builds. After that the treasurer may sell the lien at the annual sale, leaving a buyer with a claim on the house that has to be cleared before you can sell cleanly.

sections.h2: A simple order of operations for sellers
sections.html:
Start with the Assessor, because the value drives everything else. Check the Notice of Valuation that arrives by May 1, and if the number looks wrong, protest before June 8. Next, call the Treasurer to learn which halves are paid and whether any interest has started. Finally, give the title company your statement so it can request the tax certificate early.

At closing the Clerk and Recorder files the deed for $43. If you are tackling a sale from out of town, the phone numbers above cover all three offices, and the Treasurer accepts mailed payments, though only a USPS postmark counts as proof of timing.

sections.h2: Selling with tax due or a deferral
sections.html:
An outstanding balance doesn't block a sale. Back taxes, interest and any lien payoff are cleared at closing out of the price, so there is no cash to find beforehand. Before closing, the title company requests a tax certificate from the Treasurer, and the county runs an online portal for that request.

Any unpaid tax comes out of your proceeds, so the closing statement shows one payoff figure instead of several. Ask early which accounts the certificate covers, because each lien payoff adds a line to what the buyer's funds must clear.

A state property tax deferral is another matter. It is recorded as a junior lien. Repayment falls due 90 days after a sale or a contract of sale, and interest has been running since May 1 of the year it was claimed. When an owner dies and no spouse survives, repayment is due a year later.

A Delta County house that needs repairs, carries a tax lien or came through an estate can get a written cash offer from us in its current condition. Before you decide, dig out your latest statement, see whether the first half is paid and ask the title company if another lien sits ahead of the tax.

faqs.q: When is Delta County property tax due?
faqs.a: Pay in full by April 30, or in two halves due the last day of February and June 15. Amounts of $25 or less must be paid in full by April 30.

faqs.q: What is the protest deadline for a Delta County property value?
faqs.a: Real property protests are due June 8, by mail, in person or by phone. An appeal to the County Board of Equalization follows by July 15.

faqs.q: What interest does Delta County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: One percent per month under C.R.S. 39-10-104.5, with part of a month counted as a whole month. It starts March 1 for a late first half, June 16 for a late second half and May 1 for a late full payment.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Delta County?
faqs.a: Pay at the Treasurer's office at 501 Palmer Street, Suite 202, Delta, at the County Annex in Hotchkiss, by mail to PO Box 580, Grand Junction, or online through GovPros.

faqs.q: Does selling a house in Delta County end the property tax deferral?
faqs.a: A sale or contract of sale makes the state's deferral repayment due within 90 days. The deferral is a recorded junior lien, so it is paid at or soon after closing.
